Descendants of the Gods

Not merely who descended from whom, but how ancestry became authority.

Every line in this atlas is a claim. Each claim names its witnesses, the century they wrote in, and what the claim was used for. Where the sources disagree, the disagreement stays on the page.

    I · The Greek line

    From Chaos to the Argead throne

    The primordial powers, the Titans, the Olympians, and the houses that claimed them. Click a name to light its line of descent.

    II · The biblical comparison

    Judah to David

    A line that names Tamar, Rahab and Ruth. Set beside the Greek tree as a comparison, never as an identity.

    III · Tubal and the Iberian claims

    Noah to the Basques

    The ancient layer is thin. Most of the weight sits in the sixteenth century and later, and the registry says so.

    IV · The case studies

    Fifteen times ancestry was used as authority

    Each card is a claim-event from the manuscript. Open one for its witnesses, its beneficiary, and the grade the scroll prints.

    V · The witnesses in time

    Who said it first, and when

    Each small star is a claim, placed at its earliest surviving witness. Gold stars are claim-events. Rose diamonds are later receptions. The column at 700 BCE is the Theogony.

    VI · The ground

    Where the claims lived and travelled

    Beacons mark lands tied to a figure or house. Moving lines mark a claim in transit, a migration or an appeal, never a person's itinerary.
